results.prompt: Brew me a Standard deck built around Bringer of the Last Gift, Superior Spider-Man and Town Greeter.
results.text:
I'll start by checking the three requested cards and what real decks pair them with.

The three cards have no published list together. I'll check the pairs and the two archetypes that use them.

Golgari Roots is the closest real shell: it runs Town Greeter with mill and reanimation. Next I'll check the Standard legality of the mill and reanimation cards it uses, plus the suggested add-ons.

Several suggested cards are not legal in Standard (Scrapwork Mutt, Haywire Mite, Tyvar, Dread Return, Exhume), so I'll drop them. Next I'll pull the Golgari Roots reference list and check the other graveyard-recursion options.

Golgari Roots is the right shell: it runs Town Greeter, mill, and graveyard value. Superior Spider-Man needs blue, so the deck will need a small blue splash. I'll check the removal and fixing options in Standard.

Several cards I'd want are not legal here (Llanowar Wastes and Go for the Throat rotated out), so I'll confirm the rest of the removal and sideboard options before building.

I have what I need for the build. I'll run the check tool on the draft with Golgari Roots as the mana comparison.

The check flags 20 lands as light for an 8-drop deck, and the average mana value is low, so I'll move to 22 lands and trim two spells from the bottom of the curve.

The deck passes with no errors or warnings. I'll submit it as a brew with the win line and the card needs filled in.

The checker flagged three removal spells that are rarely played in Standard. I'll swap Assassin's Trophy for Maelstrom Pulse, which sees real play (2.4% of recent lists) and answers any nonland permanent. I'll keep Fell and Hero's Downfall and justify them.

I submitted a Golgari mill-and-reanimate brew with a small blue splash for Superior Spider-Man. It was accepted with no warnings.

**Direction chosen:** Golgari mill-reanimate, built on the Golgari Roots shell. I considered a Dimir version (Spider-Man and Bringer, but Town Greeter would need a green splash) and a black-green reanimation build with Xu-Ifit and Zombify. I picked Golgari because it is the only option where all three cards play naturally, and the mill from Town Greeter and Overlord feeds both Spider-Man and Bringer.

**The plan:** Mill and ramp into Bringer. Town Greeter, Overlord of the Balemurk and Dredger's Insight fill the graveyard with creatures, Llanowar Elves and Molt Tender get to eight mana, and Superior Spider-Man copies the best creature in a graveyard to mill or return again. When Bringer lands, it clears both boards and returns every creature card from both graveyards.

**Honest odds:** This is a slow deck, and the win line (Greeter, Overlord, Spider-Man, then Bringer on turn 8) has all its cards drawn by turn 8 in only 9.6% of games. It is weak against Izzet Aggro, which is 24% of the field, so expect to survive early pressure before the Bringer turn matters. The deck runs 22 lands, 3 Bringer, 3 Spider-Man and five removal spells, with a 15-card sideboard aimed at Dimir, Vivi and Rogue.

winLine.does: Turn 2: mills four, filling the graveyard with creature cards and possibly a land.
Mills four more on entering and returns a non-Avatar creature card to hand, adding fuel and a creature for the hand.
Turn 4-5: enters as a copy of Overlord or Town Greeter from a graveyard, so its ETB fires again (mill and return), and the copied card is exiled.

Turn 8 with 8 mana from lands plus Llanowar Elves and Molt Tender: each player sacrifices other creatures, then every creature card in both graveyards returns to the battlefield, leaving a 6/6 flyer with a board of returned creatures.

results.prompt: Brew me a Standard deck built around Mightform Harmonizer, Spell Snare and Full Bore.
results.text:
I'll start by checking the three requested cards and what real decks run them with.

Mightform Harmonizer and Full Bore both reward warp and landfall, but no list runs all three together. I'll check the pairs and the Harmonizer's shell.

Spell Snare's only co-occurrence data comes from Modern, so it has no Standard evidence. Full Bore appears in Boros Aggro, and Harmonizer appears in one Mono-Green list. Next I'll pull the Landfall shell and the Green reference list.

Three directions are possible: RG Landfall (Harmonizer and Full Bore, borrowing the Landfall package), UR Izzet (Spell Snare and Full Bore, borrowing Izzet Aggro), or Boros (Full Bore only). Before choosing, I'll check the exact text of the candidate cards.

I've confirmed the core cards. Screaming Nemesis shows as banned, so I'll leave it out of any build. Next I'll check the mana for the draft I have in mind, and the odds of drawing Harmonizer and Full Bore by turn 4.

The check passes with no errors. The Landfall mana warning is informational: this build runs 18 green sources to the shell's 26, because it also needs red and a blue splash. The odds are 52.8% for Harmonizer by turn 4 and 26.5% for both together, so I'm submitting it now.

I built a Red-Green Landfall deck with a light blue splash for Spell Snare, borrowing the Landfall shell's green ramp and landfall creatures to power Mightform Harmonizer. The line is Llanowar Elves for early mana, then warp Harmonizer, play a land so it doubles from 4 to 8 power, and pay R for Full Bore to give it haste and trample for an 11-damage attack on turn 4. Full Bore's haste and trample only apply to a warped creature, so Harmonizer and Nova Hellkite are the creatures it works with.

The three directions I weighed were:
- **RG Landfall (chosen):** Harmonizer and Full Bore both fit. Landfall is the only shell in the field whose ramp and landfall creatures make Harmonizer's trigger reliable.
- **UR Izzet:** This fits Spell Snare and Full Bore, but Harmonizer is green, so it doesn't fit.
- **Boros:** This fits Full Bore only.

Honest odds: Harmonizer by turn 4 on the play is 52.8%, and both Harmonizer and Full Bore together is 26.5%. The turn-4 line is the best case, not the typical one. Spell Snare is the weakest card here: it only counters mana value 2 spells, and it's in the deck as a splash card with 7 blue sources.

Warped for {2}{G} before the land drop, so it is a 4/4 on the battlefield with haste from Full Bore later.

Pay R: +3/+2 and, because Harmonizer was cast for its warp cost, trample and haste, so it attacks for 11 trample.

results.prompt: Brew me a Standard deck built around Airbender Ascension, Bramble Familiar and Appa, Steadfast Guardian.
results.text:
I built a green-white Ally deck around Airbender Ascension, Bramble Familiar and Appa, Steadfast Guardian. It's a brew, not a proven list. The closest real list is the Rogue Aang deck, which runs Appa in a blue shell and none of the other two cards. The plan is to ramp into Appa on turn 4, airbend Bramble Familiar and Llanowar Elves so they can be recast cheaply, and let the quest counters and Ally tokens build up. Elspeth, Storm Slayer then doubles the tokens and gives the team flying for the finish, around turn 6.

I considered three directions: a white-green Ally build (chosen), a white-blue Aang build borrowing Rogue's blue cards, and a mono-white airbend control deck. I picked white-green because Bramble Familiar needs green, and the Ally cards (Invasion Reinforcements, Earth King's Lieutenant, Kyoshi Warriors) feed both Appa's tokens and Airbender Ascension's counters.

The deck checks clean with 21 lands and 7 mana creatures, but the full win line is unlikely: the tool estimates all five cards appear by turn 6 in only 0.1% of games. Expect it to win through Appa and the Ally tokens more often than through the exact sequence.

winLine.does: Turn 2 mana creature and cheap body; later an airbend target Appa can exile and recast for {2}.
Flash 3/4 flyer at 4 mana; on entry airbends Bramble Familiar and Llanowar Elves so each can be recast for {2}, and each recast from exile makes a 1/1 Ally.
Each creature re-entering (and each Ally token) adds a quest counter; at four counters it blinks a creature at my end step, re-triggering Appa or Kyoshi Warriors.
Doubles all tokens (Ally, Kyoshi, Invasion); its 0 gives every creature a +1/+1 counter and flying until my next turn.
6-mana 4/4 flyer whose attack trigger airbends a permanent for recasting, the finishing flyer alongside Aang.

results.prompt: Brew me a Standard deck built around Abandon Attachments, Firebending Lesson and Combustion Technique.
results.text:
I built a red-only Lesson aggro deck around Abandon Attachments, Firebending Lesson and Combustion Technique. It's a brew, and the submission was accepted with 19 lands and a 15-card sideboard.

**Plan:** Start with cheap red creatures (Burnout Bashtronaut, Hired Claw, Emberheart Challenger), then use four Firebending Lesson, four Abandon Attachments and two Iroh's Demonstration to clear blockers and fill the graveyard with Lessons. Combustion Technique then exiles the biggest blocker, and Nova Hellkite finishes.

**Direction:** I sketched three options. Mono-red Lessons was chosen because the three requested cards and the Lesson removal are all red and fully castable on curve. The Izzet and Boros shells would have needed a second colour for little gain, and their white or blue Lessons have no recorded results. The base comes from the only Mono-Red Lesson list I found (Standard Challenge 32, placed 13th), with the red core of Izzet Aggro added. Screaming Nemesis is banned in Standard, so the Izzet and Boros lists that run it were not borrowed.

**Caveat:** The Mono-Red Lesson list is a single 13th-place result, so the deck is untested beyond that. The Inti note was answered: each Abandon discard triggers Inti to exile and let me play a card.

results.prompt: Brew me a Standard deck built around Ashling, Rekindled, Sunderflock and Bounce Off.
results.text:
The deck is submitted and accepted. It's a brew: blue-red, built around Ashling and Sunderflock, with Rogue as the donor shell.

**Plan:** Ashling flips to Rimebound on turn 3 and then adds 2 mana each turn for spells with mana value 4 or more. That mana plus a 7-drop Elemental, Mouth of the Storm, drops Sunderflock to {U}{U} on turn 6. Sunderflock then bounces every opposing non-Elemental and leaves my Elementals on the board. The deck runs about 25 Elementals so that bounce is one-sided. Bounce Off (4 copies) and Into the Flood Maw handle tempo.

**Direction chosen:** I considered three builds. A Simic Ouroboroid package shell would have needed a red splash for Ashling, and its Badgermole Cub is listed as banned in Standard. A Dimir or control build would have had too few Elementals for Sunderflock. The blue-red Elemental build keeps Ashling's red cost and blue flip cost in their natural colors, so I took it.

**Caveats:**
- The line is untested. The tools show only 6.1% of games where every card in the win line is drawn by turn 6, with no tutors simulated.
- Badgermole Cub and Stormchaser's Talent show as banned in Standard, so some field-share numbers in the menu are stale.
- Summon: Shiva and Into the Roil are in the main deck despite near-zero play rates. I kept them for specific roles (Elemental body that protects the Sunderflock turn, and instant-speed bounce), as stated in the card notes.

results.prompt: Brew me a Standard deck built around Insatiable Avarice, Doomsday Excruciator and Archenemy's Charm.
results.text:
I'll start by checking the three requested cards and what real decks pair them with.

The three requested cards are all black, and Doomsday Excruciator needs six black pips. Next I'll pull the Dimir Midrange and Reanimator shells, plus the Mono-Black results, to see what black decks run.

Three directions are on the table. Mono-Black fits the heavy black pips best. Dimir already plays Excruciator but would be short on black sources for six pips. Reanimator uses Archenemy's Charm and Avarice as recursion and tutoring. I'll pull the Mono-Black list and search the pool for black removal, draw and recursion.

The Mono-Black shell gives me a removal and creature base. I need the exact text and legality of the candidate cards before I build, so I'll look them all up in one batch.

I'm going with Mono-Black and building around the six-pip Excruciator. First I'll confirm the two sideboard sweepers I plan to use, then run the deck through the checker.

The checker passes with no errors or warnings, and the mana matches the Mono-Black reference. Submitting now.

I built a Mono-Black control deck around Doomsday Excruciator, using the Mono-Black shell from the menu (13 recent lists). The deck casts removal and grinds with Insatiable Avarice and Archenemy's Charm, then wins with Doomsday Excruciator and Bloodletter of Aclazotz. Bloodletter doubles the opponent's life loss on my turn, so one attack with Excruciator, one with Bloodletter, and an Avarice mode 2 drain on the opponent add up to 22 against 20 life.

I chose this direction over Dimir Midrange, which already plays Excruciator but would be short on the six black sources it needs, and over black-green Reanimator, which would leave Excruciator's BBBBBB to a splash. The deck has 24 black sources. Casting Excruciator is the hard part: about 45% of games will have six lands by turn 8, so expect it on turn 9 or 10.

The deck has one real risk. Excruciator mills both players to six cards, and I draw two cards a turn afterward, so I deck myself in about three turns. The win has to come fast, and Archenemy's Charm can return Excruciator if it dies. The 15-card sideboard is aimed at Dimir Midrange, Landfall and Simic Ouroboroid.

results.prompt: Brew me a Standard deck built around Iron-Shield Elf, Bloodthorn Flail and Flamewake Phoenix.
results.text:
I submitted a Rakdos (black-red) aggro brew built around the three requested cards, with 23 lands and 37 spells. No published list plays Iron-Shield Elf, Bloodthorn Flail and Flamewake Phoenix together, so this is untested.

The plan: Iron-Shield Elf and Bloodthorn Flail turn the early game into pressure, and Flamewake Phoenix is the evasive threat. Flail on Phoenix makes it a 4-power flier, which keeps Ferocious online for recursion when Phoenix dies. Terror of the Peaks, Bonehoard Dracosaur and Nova Hellkite supply the 4+ power bodies and the burn-based reach.

I considered three directions:
- **Rakdos (chosen):** The three cards split across black (Elf, Flail) and red (Phoenix), and the red aggro core from the Boros Aggro list plus black removal from Dimir Midrange covers both colours.
- **Boros with a black splash:** Elf and Flail are early black cards, so a splash would be too unreliable.
- **Dimir or Golgari midrange:** Phoenix needs RR, so it does not fit.

Odds are modest. By turn 4 on the play, each of the three is about 53% to be seen, and all three together only about 13%. The win line is turn 5 if things go right, but this is a brew, not a proven list.

Turn 5 five-drop; every creature that enters after it deals damage equal to its power to any target.
If Phoenix dies, pay R at beginning of combat while I control a 4+ power creature (Flail-equipped creature, Dracosaur, Nova, Terror) to return it from the graveyard and keep attacking in the air.

results.prompt: Brew me a Standard deck built around Resonating Lute, Inevitable Defeat and Jeskai Revelation.
results.text:
I built a Jeskai Control list with a light black splash for Inevitable Defeat, built around Resonating Lute and Jeskai Revelation. I considered three directions: straight Jeskai Control without Defeat, Jeskai with the black splash, and a Rogue-style W/R/B build. I chose the splash because Lute and Revelation only work in the Jeskai shell, and Defeat is one of the best answers available.

The plan is to land Resonating Lute on turn 4. Its mana boost applies only to instants and sorceries, so with 25 instant or sorcery spells in the deck, the lands produce 8 or more mana for Jeskai Revelation at instant speed. Revelation then bounces their best permanent, deals 4 to their face, makes two Monk tokens, draws two and gains four. Get Lost, Lightning Helix, Inevitable Defeat and No More Lies handle their threats while Stock Up and Consult the Star Charts keep card flow going.

The shell is a tuned Jeskai Control list (the 5-0 Standard League list was the reference), with three Inevitable Defeat and six black sources: four duals and two Multiversal Passage set to Swamp. The deck has about a 79% chance of a black source by turn 7 on the play. The deck has never been tested in results, so treat the splash as the main risk. The checker reports four black sources because it doesn't count the Passages; I counted them.

results.prompt: Brew me a Standard deck built around Dáin's Company, Dwarven Mauler and Kíli the Resourceful.
results.text:
I submitted a RW Dwarves and Equipment brew with Dáin's Company, Dwarven Mauler and Kíli all in the main deck. No published list plays these three together, so it is labeled a brew with Boros Aggro as the donor for its burn and mana.

**Direction chosen:** RW Storied Dwarves and Equipment. All three requested cards are RW, so this is the only direction that casts them without a splash. The other two options I weighed were mono-red with a white splash, and GW with a red splash; both would have had to splash a card that is needed early. The plan is to curve Mauler into Kíli, then feed Kíli's draw with Dwarves and Equipment entering. Mauler's discount makes its equipment nearly free, and Storied turns on Kíli's free equip. Burn (Burst Lightning, Lightning Helix, Chainsaw) clears blockers and closes the game.

**Main deck:** 4 Dwarven Mauler, 4 Dáin's Company, Kíli, Bofur, Thorin Oakenshield, Giott, Dáin Ironfoot, Fíli, Thorin Mountain-king, Minecart Daredevil, 14 Equipment (including Lost Jitte, Buster Sword, Mjölnir and 3 Chainsaw), 11 burn/removal, and 19 lands (9 Mountain, 9 Plains, Sacred Foundry).

**Caveats:**
- The checker wanted 23 lands for this low curve (average mana value 2.02). I went with 19 because the equip costs, Burst Lightning's kicker and Mjölnir are real mana sinks.
- The win line (Mauler, Kíli, Paladin's Arms, Buster Sword, Lightning Helix by turn 5) needs five specific cards. It completes by turn 5 in only about 0.1% of games, so the deck wins through a steady stream of Dwarves and Equipment rather than that exact line.
- Two cards drew checker notes, Buster Sword and Chainsaw, which no recent Standard list plays. I kept both on purpose: Buster Sword is the card-advantage Equipment that Mauler makes free to equip, and Chainsaw is removal that also counts as an artifact for Storied and as a Dwarf/Equipment target for Dáin's Company and Kíli.

results.prompt: Brew me a Standard deck built around Greedy Freebooter, The Sackville-Bagginses and Umbral Collar Zealot.
results.text:
I submitted a mono-black sacrifice brew built around the three cards. It is a brew, so no tournament list backs it, and it has not been playtested.

**Directions I weighed:**
1. **Mono-black sacrifice aristocrats (chosen).** All three requested cards are black, and the pool has enough black fodder, sacrifice payoffs and removal for 37 spells. Perfect mana also suits a deck full of one-mana plays.
2. **Dimir with the Dimir Midrange package** (Floodpits Drowner, Spyglass Siren, Requiting Hex, Bitter Triumph). It is the most-played shell in this list, but blue dilutes the sacrifice engine and needs a dozen Islands for a single splash.
3. **Mardu Discard, borrowing its Bloodghast core.** It is the strongest black-adjacent deck, but it has no room for the requested cards to be central.

I went with option 1 because it keeps the requested cards at the center and borrows only the parts that fit: Bloodghast (recurring fodder, from Mardu Discard), Overlord of the Balemurk (from Reanimator), and the cheap black removal from Dimir.

**The deck (60 cards):** 24 creatures, 13 removal and card-advantage spells, and 23 Swamps. Freebooter, Infestation Sage, Bloodghast and Common Crook supply the fodder. Zealot and Sackville are the sacrifice outlets, Vengeful Bloodwitch drains on each death, and Liliana and Vein Ripper finish. Removal is Feed the Swarm, Murder, Bitter Triumph, Requiting Hex, Eaten Alive, Corrupted Conviction and Cornered by Black Mages.

**Honest odds:** the check passed with no errors or warnings. The win line (Freebooter, then Sackville, then Zealot, then Liliana, then Vein Ripper) has all its cards by turn 7 in only about 0.3% of games. Freebooter is in the opening hand about 45% of the time, and one of Sackville or Zealot about 71% by turn 2. Treat the deck as a starting point that needs playtesting, and expect the sacrifice engine to be slow until several fodder creatures are on board.

I built a Vintage version of Legacy's Sewer Combo around Goblin Welder, Sewer-veillance Cam and Legion Extruder. It is a brew: only two Legacy lists run this shell, and none run it in Vintage.

**The plan:** Put Legion Extruder in the graveyard (Goblin Engineer's search or Melded Moxite's discard), then have Cam and Welder on the battlefield. Welder sacrifices Cam and returns Extruder, which deals 2 damage. Cam's leave trigger untaps Welder. Welder then sacrifices Extruder to return Cam, whose enter trigger untaps Welder again. That loop costs no mana and deals 2 damage per activation, so 10 activations is lethal.

**Direction:** Of the three I considered, I took a blue-red Welder loop borrowed from Legacy's Sewer Combo shell. The menu's Pyroblast and Red Elemental Blast went in as interaction against the blue-heavy field. I dropped Chaos Defiler because it needs black, and I dropped Demonic Tutor for the same reason.

The tool puts the full line drawn by turn 3 at 2.2%, so this wins through accelerants and cantrips, not reliably on curve. The 12 lands and 10 mana sources sit in line with Raker Shops. - Acceleration: Black Lotus, Mox Ruby, Mox Sapphire, Sol Ring, Mana Crypt, Mana Vault, Lotus Petal, Chrome Mox ×2

The sideboard is built to hit the field: Tormod's Crypt and Soul-Guide Lantern for Dredge and Breach, Mindbreak Trap and Abrade against the artifact decks, and Sudden Demise against white and black creatures. results.prompt: Brew me a Premodern deck built around Living Death.
results.text:
I built a black-green reanimator deck around Living Death and submitted it as a brew that borrows the Reanimator shell. Living Death can return a board of creatures in one sorcery, so I wanted reanimation spells and big creatures that make it a reset and a comeback at once. I considered three directions: the BG Survival shell where Living Death is currently played, a mono-black build using the Moneyball Black package, and the Reanimator shell. I chose the Reanimator shell because its reanimation engine (Reanimate, Exhume, Animate Dead, Dark Ritual) is the most proven in the menu, and Living Death is a mass version of that same plan.

**Plan:** Turn 3 Buried Alive puts Visara the Dreadful, Multani and Symbiotic Wurm into the graveyard. Turn 4 Dark Ritual and Living Death clear both boards and return those three creatures, and Visara starts killing blockers on turn 5. The line needs three specific cards by turn 4, and the odds of having all three are only about 7%, so the deck will often play a slower reanimation game instead. Survival of the Fittest and the reanimation spells are the backup route.

**Things to know:**
- The deck runs 15 lands plus Lotus Petal and Dark Ritual. The checker's generic warning suggested about 23 lands, but Reanimator lists run about 14, and the 6–8 mana creatures are what make the deck work.
- Living Death is also a mass reanimation for the opponent, so it is a risk when they have creatures in their graveyard.
- Living Death has almost no tournament data of its own, so the build rests on the Reanimator shell and the cards' printed text rather than a proven list.
